subject: VPC commercial: implementation credit vs platform-fee structure
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medigyhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@medigyhealth.com
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood Private for Medigy - pricing questions

Sean —

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We’re in the final stages of vendor selection and need a clearer picture on how Redwood prices Private/VPC deployments. Specifically:

- How you treat the platform fee for on-prem/VPC (amortized vs upfront).
- Support tiers and what’s included in each (SLA, response times, on-call).
- Typical discounting bands for multi-year commits (12/24/36).
- Any implementation/onboarding credits or professional services offsets you can provide for a multi-year commitment?

Quick context: we expect an initial footprint of ~8 GPU nodes at launch with steady-state ~20 nodes in year two. Security team needs a refundable usage floor? procurement@medigy will drive contracting.

If you can send a term sketch + SOW template that shows platform fee math and an example amortization, that would speed review.

Best,
Alex
Alex Jenkins
VP, Cloud Platform
Medigy Health

Attachment: none
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medigyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 13:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood Private for Medigy - pricing questions

Alex —

Really appreciate the context and the roadmap — that helps a lot. I pulled together a preliminary commercial approach that addresses each of your asks:

1) Platform fee: we typically offer an annual platform fee that can be amortized monthly on the invoice or treated as a single upfront invoice. For commitments >=24 months we discount the fee and recommend amortization for bookkeeping.

2) Support: two SKUs — Standard (business hours, 24h ticketing, best-effort critical) and Premier (24/7 critical response, 1-hr P1, assigned TAM). I’ll include a table with response times and on-call coverage.

3) Discounts: for 24-month commits we typically start at ~20% off list for node pricing; we can flex on platform fee vs implementation credit depending on your preferences.

4) Implementation credit: we can provide an implementation subsidy (one-time credit) to offset onboarding and validation costs; size depends on commit and prepay.

I’ve attached a draft term sketch that shows two options: a deeper platform-fee reduction vs a larger one-time implementation credit. Please review and tell me which structure Procurement prefers — simpler bookkeeping (amortized platform fee) or higher one-time onboarding credit.

If it helps, I can loop in Karthik on acceptable discount guardrails and have Marissa draft the SOW.

–Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Medigy_TermSketch_v1.pdf (term sketch, pricing scenarios)
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medigyhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@medigyhealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood Private for Medigy - pricing questions

Thanks Sean — quick clarifying notes from our side: 

- Procurement would prefer lower platform fee in year one only (easier for our Opex planning) rather than amortizing a large upfront fee.
- Alternatively we’d accept a larger onboarding credit if that avoids a weighted platform fee on our P&L.
- On support: we want the Premier SLA for the first 6 months of launch and then to re-evaluate.
- Can you include a SOW template and an approximate PoC timeline (we’d like a 6–8 week validation).

Contracts wants the term sketch in a PDF and the SOW as an editable doc.

Alex

Attachment requested: SOW template (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Medigy pricing — internal alignment

Sean / Monica —

A few thoughts before we send a formal counter:

- Tradeoff idea: reduce platform fee by 10% in year one (Redwood absorbs some fixed cost) + offer a $60k implementation credit applied to the first invoice. That preserves predictable invoicing but gives the customer upfront relief.
- If they push for a larger credit we can go to $75k but it must be contingent on a minimum 18-month commit and 50% prepay of first-year run-rate.
- Guardrails from pricing: max 25% off node list pricing, implementation credits capped at $75k for named enterprise deals, platform fee concessions require minimum commit and at least 40% prepay.
- Support: for Premier (requested) add a one-time onboarding TAM fee of $15k (covers runbook, playbook, and 2 weeks embedded support). This can be credited against implementation credit if they want.

If this looks ok I’ll have a term sheet (editable) and an SOW draft ready — Marissa to own SOW. Karthik, can you confirm the guardrails are acceptable?

— Marissa

On Wed, Jul 28, 2026 at 11:52 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Looks fine. Confirming: pricing team approves up to 25% discount on node/unit rates, platform fee concessions up to 15% year-one reduction, and implementation credits up to $75k. Must require >=12 months and prefer >=18 months for larger credits. 50% prepay required for credits > $50k.
>
> Karthik
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medigyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Commercial proposal: Medigy VPC pilot + 18-month commitment

Alex —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on internal guardrails we can do the following offer:

Summary (final commercial sketch)
- Commitment: 18-month term for Private (VPC/on-prem) with option to renew at pre-agreed rates.
- Node pricing: 22% off list for node/unit pricing (applies to GPU node-hours).
- Platform fee: 10% reduction year-one only, amortized monthly for bookkeeping.
- Implementation credit: $60,000 one-time credit applied to first invoice. If Medigy prefers a larger credit ($75k), we require 50% prepay of first-year run-rate.
- Support: Premier for first 6 months (1-hr P1, 24/7 critical response, assigned TAM). Premier is priced at +15% of the platform fee; we will credit $15,000 TAM onboarding fee against the implementation credit.
- PoC timeline: target 6–8 weeks from kick-off, SOW attached for scope and milestones.

Next steps: I’ve attached an editable term sketch and SOW (see attachments). If Procurement is OK, I can route to Legal for DocuSign prep. Please confirm whether you prefer the $60k credit + 10% platform reduction or to push for $75k with the associated prepay requirement.

Doc links: [DocuSign will be used for the signature step — once commercial is approved we’ll open the envelope].

Thanks,
Sean
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Medigy_VPC_TermSheet_v3.pdf, SOW_Draft.docx
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@medigyhealth.com>

Cc: contracts@medigyhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial proposal: Medigy VPC pilot + 18-month commitment

Sean —

Thanks — this is helpful and closer to what we need. A couple quick asks from Procurement/legal: 

1) Can we instead do a 12-month commit with quarterly invoicing? We’re sensitive to locking cash for 18 months.
2) Please provide the editable term sketch and SOW (docx) to contracts@medigyhealth.com — they’ll run the redlines and come back.
3) We’ll need an approximate PoC calendar (week-by-week) embedded in the SOW so our engineering team can resource it; 6 weeks is preferable.

If you can accept 12 months at the following adjustments we can move quickly: keep the 22% node discount, revert to $60k credit, and change platform fee reduction to a one-time $25k discount applied to invoice 1 (instead of amortized). Procurement will review and escalate if necessary.

I’ll get contracts@medigy to review and respond with any redlines.

— Alex
